name: Timothy, with Lois and Eunice
charge: Unfeigned faith that dwelt first in his grandmother and his mother; knowing the holy scriptures from a child
summary: A boy of Lystra with a Greek father and a believing Jewish mother had been taught the scriptures from a child by two women. Paul found him well reported of, circumcised him for the Jews' sake, and took him. He became Paul's own son in the faith, the man he trusted with Ephesus, and the one he wrote his last letter to.
offense: When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also. From a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation. Timotheus was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium. I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state. For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ's. But ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel.
judgment: Him would Paul have to go forth with him. Timothy, my own son in the faith. This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare. Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery. The blessing on the two women's teaching is the man it made: named in the address of six epistles, and left in charge of the church at Ephesus.

entries.commentary: These are the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments, commanded to be taught, that thou mightest fear the Lord thy God: the fear always comes up first, thou, and thy son, and thy son's son, all the days of thy life. Hear therefore, O Israel, and observe to do it, that ye may increase mightily. Increase and power are the desire of the people, and keeping the commandments is the one thing our people have not tried; assimilation, the gods of the nations, and politics, liberal or conservative, have all been tried and none of it has worked. The land that floweth with milk and honey is the true riches: cattle, vegetation, agriculture, land to cultivate, the gift that keeps on giving.

Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children: diligently means you do not miss a beat. The children are not to be taught the dance challenges, halloween, and the satanic birthdays, and remember that you teach by your actions, so you fix yourself first. Talk of them when thou sittest in thine house: go through the scriptures at home, the histories of Samson, Joseph, Solomon, and David. When thou walkest by the way: when you run into each other, ask, are you keeping the laws, what four chapters did you read today? When thou liest down, and when thou risest up: the bedtime stories are biblical, the ten plagues of Egypt rather than the fairy tales, prayer before they sleep and when they rise, and even the coloring books painting the images brown, bringing it back to its true course.

Thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes: bind them in your mind. The commandments are the light, the torch that guides you and leads you in the correct path. And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates.

When the Lord brings thee into great and goodly cities which thou buildedst not, houses full of all good things which thou filledst not, wells digged which thou diggedst not, and thou shalt have eaten and be full, then beware lest thou forget the Lord which brought thee forth out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name; ye shall not go after the gods of the people round about you, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God, lest his anger be kindled and destroy thee from off the face of the earth. Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah.

Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes. Testimony is one of the trigger words that confuses our people: the laws are what Moses gave, and the testimonies are the history of the forefathers and foremothers, what they went through and how it was handled according to the laws. Everything correlates: when king David had Uriah killed, that goes back to thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not covet, and bearing false witness; he was dealing with much sin in that one matter. That is how you go precept upon precept, line upon line, to the law and to the testimony. A personal testimony that cannot come back to the Bible is not biblical; if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light, no truth, in them. Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, what mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments? The children will ask why David did what he did, why Samson, why Miriam was judged, why Moses was barred; the answer starts with the history. Then thou shalt say unto thy son, we were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out with a mighty hand, and shewed signs and wonders upon Egypt and upon Pharaoh; he brought us out that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he sware unto our fathers. The Most High always keeps his covenant; he is not a man, that he should lie. The Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive: the fear again stands first, and the commandments are for Israel's good and preservation, obligated and not optional, with punishment for breaking and reward for keeping. And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments: keeping the commandments is what makes you righteous, and righteousness is kept at all times, the fringes worn seven days a week and not on the sabbath only. Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.

A good name goes into your reputation, and your reputation is more important than how much money you have. You can have a lot of money and be a dirtbag, the scum of the earth, and nobody respects you. It is about how you treated people and how you impacted their lives. A rich man everybody dislikes will be forgotten when he dies. It is not about money. The rich and poor meet together; the Most High is the maker of them all.

A prudent man foresees the evil and hides himself. In marriage, when your spouse has a frustrated spirit, a prudent person deals with it wisely and uses choice words to de-escalate instead of coming in guns blazing. Out in the world you observe the time. At the basketball court two dudes started trash talking, then it got personal, and foreseeing the evil he grabbed his stuff and left. Afterward he learned one pulled a knife and chased the other around the court. A brother said his coworker wanted to learn the Bible and he would go teach her alone. Not a good idea. One thing led to another, the Bible ended up under the bed, and they committed the deed. A righteous man foresees the evil and does not sit alone in a house with an attractive woman. The flesh takes over and the spirit leaves, so be mindful of the situations you put yourself in. By humility and the fear of the Most High are riches, honor, and life.

Thorns and snares are in the way of the forward; he that keeps his soul is far from them. The simple do not foresee the evil, destruction, or judgment coming, so they carry on and end up caught up in child support, domestic violence charges, or crossfire. Train up a child in the way he should go. Children are like a blank canvas; whatever you put into them and whatever they witness growing up is the type of person they become, unless some intervention happens. He trains his ten-year-old son and eight-year-old daughter in the commandments, honesty, against lying, and against laziness. They have chores after school: homework, clean the room, dishes, laundry. It builds character so they are not lazy. At first you have to repeat yourself, but it becomes automatic. Then they have the rest of the evening to play or enjoy themselves. You must hold your children accountable. Kids with too much liberty get pregnant young or get involved in gang violence and jail, because they were not trained up properly. When he is old he will not depart from it, because you instilled these qualities while he was young.

The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender. He that sows iniquity will reap vanity, and the rod of his anger will fail. He that has a bountiful eye will be blessed, for he gives of his bread to the poor. This is the brother who is not selfish and is very giving.

Cast out the scorner and contention goes out. A scorner always has a problem with everything: "why are we eating chicken, why not beef; why water, why no juice." Nothing is ever good enough. Get rid of that person and you have peace. He that loves pureness of heart, for the grace of his lips the king will be his friend. The eyes of the Most High preserve knowledge, and he overthrows the words of the transgressor.

The slothful man says there is a lion outside, I will be slain in the streets. There is no lion; it is an excuse not to do something because of the possibility something might go wrong. Scared money does not make money. This type of brother sits on his hands: "I might get in a car accident, it is too cold, I might get frostbite, it is too hot, I might get sunburned." One brother would not take off his cap for the Bible because he might get pneumonia. The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit; he that is abhorred of the Most High falls in. Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child, but the rod of correction drives it far from him. You have to discipline and correct your child, including spankings, not beating the hell out of him. He that oppresses the poor to increase his riches will come to want. This is exploiting the poor, like setting up nail shops and corner stores in our communities with the glass you have to slide your money through.

Bow down your ear and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to knowledge. It is pleasant if you keep them within you. These excellent things and counsels are written to make you know the certainty of the words of truth, so you may answer the words of truth to them that send to you.

Rob not the poor because he is poor, neither oppress the afflicted, for the Most High will plead their cause and spoil the soul of those that spoil them. Make no friendship with an angry man, and with a furious man do not go, because he will turn and fight you, disrespect you, and get you in trouble. He starts mess and you have to fight to defend him. Do not befriend a furious man lest you learn his ways and get a snare to your soul. When you hang around certain people their spirit rubs off. Brothers start to talk like each other; a woman not into something picks it up from sisters who are. Be mindful of who you hang around.

Be not one that strikes hands or is surety for debts. If you have nothing to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you. Remove not the ancient landmark which your fathers have set. See a man diligent in business; he will stand before kings, not before mean men. To deal among the upper echelon you have to be diligent. -

verses.text: I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with pure conscience, that without ceasing I have remembrance of thee in my prayers night and day;
Greatly desiring to see thee, being mindful of thy tears, that I may be filled with joy;
When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also.
Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands.
But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them;
And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.
All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:
Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timotheus shortly unto you, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.
For I have no man likeminded, who will naturally care for your state.
For all seek their own, not the things which are Jesus Christ’s.
But ye know the proof of him, that, as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel.
Unto Timothy, my own son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our Father and Jesus Christ our Lord.
This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare;
Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery.
Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all.
Take heed unto thyself, and unto the doctrine; continue in them: for in doing this thou shalt both save thyself, and them that hear thee.
And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
